rationale: workflow-use is a deterministic browser automation workflow framework (RPA 2.0) built on top of browser-use. It provides semantic-only element finding with multi-strategy fallback (7 strategies: text_exact, role_text, aria_label, placeholder, title, alt_text, text_fuzzy), a SelectorGenerator for self-healing selectors, and LLM-assisted workflow generation from natural language prompts. Relevance score 6.5/10: moderate-to-high relevance to scraping pipeline concerns (browser-automation, self-healing, script-generation via LLM, fuzzy matching via SequenceMatcher). Tier B because the source is substantial (83 Python files, ~3230-line semantic executor alone) with 25 test files and a complete browser extension recorder, but lacks production-hardening (README explicitly warns 'early development'), has no architecture/design documents, and is a single contributor project around browser-use. The four affected concerns are confirmed via source: (1) browser-automation via browser-use integration and Playwright-based element finding, (2) self-healing via fallback strategy chains in SelectorGenerator and ElementFinder, (3) script-generation via HealingService.generate_workflow_from_prompt() and BuilderService using LLM, (4) fuzzy-matching via SequenceMatcher-based text_fuzzy strategy in element_finder.py. Not affected: jsonld-extraction, queue, stealth, fulltext-search (no source evidence found for any of these).
limitations: Not a declared Veridian core-candidate; no heritage claim established
Early development stage (README self-describes as 'very early development, not recommended for production')
No architecture or design documentation (no ADR, no ARCHITECTURE.md, no design docs found)
Fuzzy matching is a single SequenceMatcher call (difflib), not a dedicated fuzzy-matching subsystem
No standalone queue/job scheduling system; only an internal asyncio.Queue for event processing in the recorder service
No stealth or anti-bot detection evasions
Heavily dependent on browser-use as runtime; not usable as a standalone scraping framework
LLM-dependent for variable extraction and workflow building despite 'deterministic' conversion path
Single-owner project (Gregor Zunic) with limited contributor base
Tests exist (25 test files) but no CI test runner visible (only lint.yml in .github/workflows)
Storage is file-based JSON/YAML, no database backend
No versioned API or backwards-compatibility guarantees documented
